input.question: What was popular British opinion of the American Revolution?
input.ground_truth: Something that could be used to gauge popular opinion in that time was voting in the House of Commons. The last time any PM was defeated over issue of war and peace (until David Cameron on Syria) was in 1782 regarding the rebellious American colonies.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What was popular British opinion of the American Revolution?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big family with cousins who live far away. One day, your cousins decide they want to make their own rules and don’t want to listen to the family’s old rules anymore. Some of your family back home (in Britain) think, “Hey, that’s not fair! They should still listen to us because we’re their family and we helped them grow up.” So, a lot of people in Britain thought the American cousins were being naughty for wanting to leave and make their own country.

Some British people were mad at the Americans, and some didn’t care much. But many thought the Americans should stay part of the big family (the British Empire) and follow the old rules. Only a few British people thought the Americans should be allowed to leave and do their own thing.

So, most British people didn’t like the idea of the American Revolution—they wanted the colonies to stay with Britain.
